title: Limbic structures take part in emotion, the amygdala especially in fear
summary: OpenStax says the limbic system, including the hypothalamus, thalamus, amygdala, and hippocampus, is involved in emotion and memory, and that the amygdala is studied especially for fear and anxiety.
body: OpenStax Psychology describes the limbic system as a brain area involved in emotion and memory. It includes the hypothalamus, which plays a role in turning on the sympathetic nervous system during an emotional reaction; the thalamus, a sensory relay toward the amygdala and cortex; the amygdala, which processes emotional information and sends it on; and the hippocampus, which ties emotional experience to cognition. The page says the amygdala has received a great deal of research attention for fear and anxiety. This is a textbook map of those structures. It is not a scan result for any one person.
